title: Data
description: The back-office table on twelve real rows of the proposals view, with its sorting, action menu and pagination. A three-row demonstration table proves nothing: neither the density, nor the alignment of numbers, nor what becomes of a column of long titles.

table.title: Proposal list
table.note: Density is deliberate: these people read negotiation documents, a well-composed table does not put them off. Sorting is controlled by the screen, never by the table — sorting inside the component would produce a wrong ranking as soon as data is paginated server-side. Below 640 px, secondary columns disappear: the page body never scrolls horizontally.
table.caption: Proposals submitted for COP31, with their review progress

pagination.title: Pagination
pagination.note: The total count comes before the page numbers: it is what tells you whether the filter bit. The sliding window avoids twenty tab stops between the list and the footer; below 640 px, only “previous” and “next” remain.

empty.title: Table with no results
empty.note: A table left empty because a filter returns nothing NEVER offers to create something: it offers to widen the search. Confusing the two is how duplicates are manufactured — the costliest flaw of the previous platform.
empty.caption: Proposals matching the active filters
empty.stateDescription: Forty proposals exist for this edition. Widen the search or remove a filter.
